transcript: Blackout Songs by Joe White is about dependency and a relentless search for clarity no matter the cost. When these two people meet at an AA meeting, their immediate connection sparks a years-long journey in and out of each other's lives, underscored by recovery and relapse. I really like the slow burn nature of this story and the way that it withholds information. Although that occasionally causes some confusion in the timeline, the blurriness feels thematically apt and makes for a juicy assignment for the actors in that there's lots of blanks to fill in. I didn't find either of the characters super riveting, but the emotional journey of both of them was interesting enough, and I felt the emotional peak was very earned. That said, in the aftermath of my viewing, I do find myself wondering what this piece is really trying to say. is it an appraisal of love even in the midst of pain? Perhaps a cautionary tale about conflating connection with enablement? Or is it simply a devastating portrait of alcoholism? Whatever the case, its meaning will probably be subject to the eye of the beholder. With that, another program for my collection.
